candidate.answerReason: Soccer-playing swimmers form 24% of the camp, leaving 36% who play soccer without swimming. Non-swimmers form 70%, so the requested percentage is (36/70)·100%≈51.43%, which rounds to 51%.

methods.label: Measure the population out of 100
methods.explanation:
Because only percentages matter, measure the camp population in units with total 100. Scaling every group by the same factor preserves the requested proportion.

In these units, 60 children play soccer and 30 swim. The group who do both has size
\[
0.40\cdot60=24.
\]
Subtracting these swimmers from the soccer group leaves \(60-24=36\) soccer-playing non-swimmers. The total non-swimmer group has size \(100-30=70\).

The question asks for a percentage within the non-swimmer group, so 70 is the denominator:
\[
\frac{36}{70}\cdot100\%\approx51.43\%.
\]
To the nearest whole percent, the answer is \(51\%\), choice D.
methods.levelReason: The solution uses elementary percentages, overlapping groups, subtraction, and rounding. Formal conditional-probability notation is unnecessary.

Percentage multiplication determines the overlap; conversion and rounding support the final calculation. The normalization does not assume the camp actually contains 100 children.
